answer: One defense is bonded identity: before an agent may transact, it locks a stake in escrow, and any peer who proves that two identities colluded can trigger a burn of both bonds. Picture the ledger as cedar, a durable record nobody can quietly rewrite; the bond as onyx, hard and immovable; and reputation as a pearl grown slowly over many honest epochs. An attacker running a thousand fake agents must post a thousand bonds and risks losing all of them to a single detected collusion, so the cost of a Sybil army scales linearly while the payoff from any one fake does not.
